newsitem.title: USA: Brent still lurks in US Gulf despite narrower arb.
newsitem.headline: Brent still lurks in US Gulf despite narrower arb.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude oil continued to lurk in the U.S. Gulf Coast on Tuesday despite a narrowing transatlantic arbitrage, traders said.
Activity was light as traders returned to work in the wake of the U.S. Memorial Day holiday.
A U.S. company was offering the benchmark grade at around 65 cents a barrel under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for delivery July 7-12, traders said.
A trading house not usually associated with delivered barrels was also showing Brent at around the same discount for July 1-10 arrival.
For most Gulf Coast companies, transatlantic barrels were still priced attractively despite the narrower arb. "At 65 cents under (WTI), it's still a pretty good deal," one said.

For at least one major U.S. buyer, however, the arb was closed. "Nothing is working at the moment...LLS (Light Louisiana Sweet) is readily available and fairly weak right now," he said, referring to the key domestic alternative to Brent.
The July spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.50-55 a barrel Tuesday afternoon, shrinking around 15-20 cents from last week, traders said.
In Europe, a trading house sold a dated Brent cargo at July Brent plus nine cents a barrel fob to another trading house for June 11-13 loading.

From West Africa, a U.S. company and a Swiss-based trader were heard offering Nigerian Qua Iboe crude, each asking around dated Brent plus $1.95 a barrel for delivery at the end of June and early July, respectively.
Hints that Asian crudes may be making their way into the Gulf Coast continued to surface, with Indonesian Widuri and Minas the latest grades heard discussed.
The unusual talk of Asian barrels moving into the U.S. Gulf prompted speculation of a slowdown in Far East buying.
From Latin America, the results of Colombian Ecopetrol's latest tender for Cusiana were eagerly awaited for either late Tuesday or early Wednesday.
The cargo is now scheduled to load June 23-24. Ecopetrol had shifted the dates from June 17-18 after failing to receive an acceptable bid in an initial tender last week.
The sweet grade was last sold at $1.23 a barrel under WTI/Cushing on an fob basis.
One trader speculated that the narrower arbitrage would spark more interest in Cusiana.
"(Ecopetrol) will probably get a little more attentiveness because of the arb. The buyers and sellers are running towards each other," he said.
For July loading, a total of seven cargoes are on tap, with Ecopetrol holding four: July 6-10, July 15-19, July 24-28 and July 28-August 1.
Equity producer British Petroleum has two: July 10-14 and July 20-24, while fellow equity holder Total has one around July 30-August 1.
From Ecuador, a trading house is showing Oriente crude for end-July to early August delivery, asking around $3.25 a barrel under WTI/Cushing fob.
The grade was sold into the Gulf last week around $3.28 under WTI/Cushing on an fob basis.

Meanwhile, state Petrolecuador opened a purchase tender for 2.6 million barrels of diesel fuel for delivery from June to December to cover the planned closure of the 90,000 barrel per day (bpd) Esmeraldas refinery, trade sources said.
The refinery is slated to be shut down from mid-June to mid-August to complete a planned capacity expansion to 110,000 bpd.
Elsewhere in Latin America, Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP plans to open a tender this Friday to buy one million barrels of crude for delivery at the end of July.
The company is seeking crude with an API gravity of 29-42 degrees.
--Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
